sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside Pi-Bolt, a build of pi (a coding agent harness) compiled ahead of time. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.addendum:
<addendum>
Think concisely. Keep internal reasoning brief and focused on the immediate step.
Output tool calls directly without conversational filler.
</addendum>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, relative to path, e.g. '*.ts', 'src/**/*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'. A pattern without '/' matches file names at any depth

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

Running the store tests separately to isolate failures. The bump-phone tests appear to time out because of sleep() calls. I will examine the bump-phone source more carefully.

The test command timed out after 60 seconds. I will increase the timeout and run the store tests first. The bump-phone issue is that closing the dialog resets the list to top. The current walkPass scrolls to bottom, then swipes back upward to process cards.

The bump-phone code does not track list position independently. It reads the screen each iteration. After backToSales resets the list to the top, the loop continues upward from the previous position. This causes the walkPass to process the wrong cards.

The cooldown skip path does not set `reread`. The dump snapshot remains stale. The loop then tries to process another card on the same screen. The list has already reset to the top. This mismatch causes the failure.

The bump-one skip path does not set `reread`. The list resets to the top after the back press, but the loop continues with the stale dump snapshot. The pending items are spread across different screens, so only one card is processed per dump.

The bottom scroll requires three swipes to reach the final page. The walkPass loop processes the last card on that page, which triggers a cooldown skip. The list resets to the top after the back press, but the loop continues with the stale dump snapshot.

The walkPass loop continues after the cooldown skip. It swipes back upward, but the list remains at the top because the back press already reset it. The dump snapshot is still stale, so the loop processes the wrong cards. It then scrolls back to the top again, and the stuck detection finally triggers after two consecutive identical dumps.

The second pass scrolls to the bottom again. It then walks upward, dropping the list by two cards each time. After two swipes, the screen shows cards 4 and 5, both of which are pending. The loop processes them in reverse order.

The fake adb tap logic uses the current `top` value to resolve coordinates. After the back press resets `top` to zero, the tap for the stale dump card lands in the wrong slot. The test harness therefore fails to find the expected card, causing the failure.

The tapped assertion passed, so the stale-dump tap did not land on the wrong card. I am re-reading bumpOne to find the actual failure.

The `dumpXml` function may return a cached screen because of `SCREEN_REUSE_MS`. This would explain why the stale-dump tap assertion passed despite the list resetting to the top.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
The shelf seed data has null values for bumpAgoDays and bumpCount.

recordCooldown leaves bumped_at and bump_count null. replaceFromPhone computes bumpCount from the card, estimates next_bump_at as roughly 3 days later, and laterOf keeps the observed cooldown. A one-hour cooldown test case is also being considered.

replaceFromPhone with bumpCount 3 and 10-minute ago sets bumpedAt to now minus 10 minutes. The estimate lands roughly 96 hours later, which is later than the observed one-hour cooldown, so laterOf returns the estimate. In the prior-match case, the new estimate falls to November 10th, which is already past the current timestamp.

A heuristic is being considered to distinguish observations from estimates. If the prior next_bump_at matches the estimate derived from the prior bumpedAt and bumpCount, it is treated as an estimate and discarded. Otherwise it is treated as an observation. The recordCooldown case has null prior values, so the prior next is treated as an observation.

Old estimates are never preserved, even when they are later than the new estimate. If the phone text omits the bumpedAt, the prior bumpedAt should be kept and next_bump_at recomputed from it. The test for this case does not verify next_bump_at.

A concrete `ingestedNextBumpAt` function is being drafted. It computes the next bump time from the new bumpedAt and bumpCount when both are present, otherwise returns null. The author notes that the test case includes ago text, so bumpedAt changes rather than being kept from the prior.

The `isObservation` helper is being defined. It returns true when the prior next_bump_at is missing, when bumped_at or bump_count is absent, or when the prior next does not match the estimate derived from the prior bumpedAt and bumpCount. This means that an explicit nextBumpAt from recordBump is treated as an observation.

recordBump without an explicit nextBumpAt sets next equal to the estimate, so it is not treated as an observation. recordCooldown overwrites next_bump_at with the observed value, which will not match the estimate, so it is correctly treated as an observation. A coincidental match between the observed value and the estimate is unlikely and untested.

The next replaceFromPhone call correctly handles both estimate and observation cases. A day-level bumpedAt preservation edge case is noted, but the relevant test only checks bumpedAt and not nextBumpAt.

Keeping the prior bumpedAt and bumpCount produces an estimate identical to the prior next, so the logic correctly discards it as an estimate rather than preserving it.

The day-level matching case is being examined more carefully. The test sets bumpAgoMinutes to null while bumpAgoDays is 5, but production parseCaption always sets both fields together for day-based phrases. The store function currently derives minutes from days when minutes is null.

When bumpAgoMinutes is null but bumpAgoDays is set, the prior bumpedAt should be kept if its age floors to the same number of days. If bumpAgoMinutes is provided, the precise calculation must be used even when it matches the day-derived value. Otherwise a real parser case like "끌올 5일 전" would lose the precise prior time.

The test intentionally sets bumpAgoMinutes to null to simulate day-only input, since the production parser always supplies both fields. The implementation is being drafted as an `ingestedBumpedAt` function that checks whether the prior bumpedAt matches the day bucket when minutes are absent.

The `ingestedBumpedAt` implementation is being drafted. It returns the prior bumpedAt when minutes are absent and the prior age matches the day bucket. Otherwise it computes the bumpedAt from minutes or days. A `sameDayAgo` helper checks if the prior age floors to the target days. The author is questioning whether the matching window should be exactly [days, days+1) or something else.

Both UTC floor and Seoul timezone calendar-day calculations correctly match the target day bucket for the test cases. The choice between them does not affect the results.

Flooring the age to whole days is chosen over rounding, since it matches the existing day-based calculation and is more standard for "N일 전". A tolerance window around the computed instant is also being considered.

The function comment clarifies that observations must not be moved earlier by estimates. The new test ensures that old estimates are not treated as observations simply because they are later.

No database schema changes are needed. The heuristic approach avoids migrations. The comment should be updated to reflect the new logic.

A dedicated `next_bump_observed` column is now being considered instead of the heuristic. The comment "관측만 지킨다" suggests explicit observation tracking is more reliable than inference. The proposed schema would mark cooldowns and explicit bumps as observed, while estimates would be marked as unobserved.

The heuristic approach is being abandoned in favor of a dedicated `next_bump_observed` column. A subtle bug in the inference logic is being identified.

The `next_bump_observed` column is being abandoned. A concrete scenario is being traced to verify the heuristic: after recordBump sets an estimate next, replaceFromPhone computes a new estimate T2 that is earlier than T1 and stores it. The author notes that T2 will again match the estimate derived from the new bumpedAt and count, so it remains an estimate. They also confirm that recordCooldown correctly preserves its observed value because the prior bumpedAt is null.

The heuristic logic is confirmed correct for edge cases. When bumpCount changes but bumpedAt stays the same, the old estimate is replaced by a new estimate for the updated count. When bumpCount or bumpedAt changes while preserving a later observation, the existing test already covers this. The implementation plan for store.ts is now being drafted.

The `ingestedBumpedAt` function is being implemented. It returns the prior bumpedAt when minutes are absent and the prior age matches the target day bucket. Otherwise it computes the bumpedAt from minutes or days. A `dayAgoMatches` helper is also being drafted to validate that the prior timestamp is valid and not in the future.

The `dayAgoMatches` helper is finalized using `Math.floor((now - at) / 86_400_000) === days`. The existing minutes-based calculation will be kept for consistency. `replaceFromPhone` will be extended to pass `priorBumpedAt` and `priorBumpCount` into `ingestedNextBumpAt` so the heuristic can distinguish observations from estimates.

The `ingestedNextBumpAt` function is being drafted. It computes the estimate from the new bumpedAt and bumpCount, then returns that estimate if the prior next is not an observation. Otherwise it keeps the later of the prior observation and the new estimate. The comment clarifies that only the phone's reported next bump time counts as an observation; estimates are not preserved even when they are later.

The `observedNext` helper is being drafted. It returns true when `bumpedAt` or `bumpCount` is missing, or when the stored `next` does not match the current estimate. The author is verifying that `estimateNextBumpAt` returns an ISO string identical to the one stored by `recordBump`, ensuring exact string comparison works.

The failing test's expected next bump time is correctly earlier than the current time. The author is now turning to the bump-phone test failures, specifically the swipe optimization and home screen detection. They will also check whether changing `backToSales` affects other tests and how home screen detection is handled elsewhere.

The second failing test lands on the Karrot home screen after closing the dialog, so pressing back again exits the app. The fix is to detect when the app is not on the sales screen and reopen sales via deep link instead of pressing back. The current `backToSales` function only checks for "판매관리" and "그만두기" in the XML dump.

The first test works with a single back press because the app returns to the sales list. The second test fails because pressing back again after landing on the home screen exits the app entirely. The fix is to detect the home screen and reopen sales via deep link instead of pressing back.

The home screen can be distinguished from the bump sheet by checking the XML dump for the absence of "판매관리", "그만두기", and cooldown text, while presence of "홈" or "나의 당근" indicates the home feed. If the app lands on the home screen or has already exited to Kakao, the test should reopen sales via deep link instead of pressing back again.

The `backToSales` algorithm is being refined. After closing the cooldown tip, one back press should exit the sheet. If the next dump still lacks the sales list, the app is on the home feed or elsewhere, so the test should reopen sales via deep link instead of pressing back again.

The author is checking whether "홈" can appear on the sales screen and if the fake server handles the karrot://my_sales deep link. They must ensure stray.swipes stays zero by reopening sales before any swipe occurs. The first test's swipe count also needs verification.

The walk logic is being refined to avoid wasted upward swipes. After an action that returns to the sales list, the list may have jumped to the top. The current code continues the inner card loop with the old dump, which can cause a "gone" return and then walk upward from the top until stuck. The desired behavior is to abort the upward walk and go straight to the bottom again when the list has reset or the visible cards have changed.

The simpler approach is chosen. After any action that calls backToSales, the walk will restart from the bottom. This matches the comment that closing the window resets the list to the top, so continuing the upward walk on the stale dump is unnecessary.

Restarting from the bottom after each processed item would require 13 swipes for three items, exceeding the 12-swipe limit. The author is weighing this trade-off against the safety of re-reading the list after every action.

A single bottom fling cannot reliably reach the bottom like scrollToEdge does, so that shortcut is rejected. The author is now looking for other ways to save at least one swipe and stay within the 12-swipe limit.

The author realized that `scrollToEdge` can be shortened by reducing its stuck confirmation from two to one swipe. This would bring the total to ten swipes for five items and pass the limit. They are also considering whether to skip confirmation after a recent edge fling. The test comment about jumping to the top and avoiding wasted upward walks suggests the fix may need to span both `scrollToEdge` and `walkPass`.

The phrase "바로 맨 아래로 간다" is interpreted as a direct bottom fling rather than a walk. The author is now designing an algorithm that produces at most 12 swipes total. They are also considering whether the fake server's swipe input lands directly on the edge, which would make the three confirmation swipes in `scrollToEdge` unnecessary.

The fake server settles the list with a single bottom fling, but a real device needs the stuck-loop confirmation. Because the test counts every swipe including confirmation, the author is now enumerating a minimal correct sequence that fits within the 12-swipe budget.

A concrete seven-swipe sequence for the three items is now mapped out. After each processed item, the list resets to the top, so the algorithm can restart from the bottom instead of continuing the upward walk. This avoids wasted upward swipes and stays well under the 12-swipe limit.

The author is now weighing whether to lower the `scrollToEdge` stuck threshold from two to one swipe. This would bring the total to ten swipes and pass the limit, but they are checking if the "진전이 없으면" test still works with only one confirmation swipe.

The test contains only one swipe count assertion.

walkUp always calls scrollToEdge, so the test fails. I'll modify walkPass to handle re-bottoming after a jump with a single fling instead of three swipes.

The plan is to have walkPass fling to the bottom once after detecting a reset, then continue the same pass instead of returning. This yields 9 swipes total and avoids changing the stuck threshold.

A single fling after a reset might not reach the bottom on a long list. The safer approach is to call scrollToEdge again after the jump, but reduce its confirmation threshold to stuck>=1 so it fits the swipe budget. Reliability is more important than a single cheap swipe.

A `knownEdge` parameter could let scrollToEdge skip redundant confirmation after a single fling. This avoids triple-confirming and keeps the pass within budget.

The `knownEdge` approach is now the chosen solution. After the first pass records the bottom head, subsequent trips after a reset use only one swipe to reach it. This yields exactly nine swipes total. The stuck threshold stays at two for unknown edges. If the bottom item changes, the known edge mismatch falls back to normal confirmation.

Reset detection will compare the post-action card list against the pre-action state. If the processed card is missing and the key changed, walkPass returns early. walkUp then restarts the pass, and scrollToEdge uses the known bottom title for a single swipe.

scrollToEdge will return the settled bottom card title. When that title matches the known edge, the function returns immediately without extra confirmation swipes.

Always restarting after an action would still work, but it wastes a swipe when the screen is static. Restarting only when the screen actually changes is the better approach.

The "gone" state after an action signals a list reset. The current code continues walking up from a stale dump instead of restarting. Re-reading the screen after each action and comparing it to the pre-action state will catch these resets and restart the pass cleanly.

The implementation now compares the post-action card list against the pre-action list. If the processed card is missing or the key changed, the pass ends immediately. This cleanly handles both the "gone" state and window-close resets.

The "gone" state is only for the next item on a stale dump, not the item just processed. Re-reading after a skip or cooldown returns the same list, so the pass continues cleanly without restarting.

The landHome case is handled cleanly: after reopening sales, the pass ends because the card list changed, and the next pass uses the known bottom edge with a single fling.

If openSales fails and the app remains on home, stray swipes would occur. backToSales must verify it is actually on the sales screen before returning, or the walk should not swipe until it is.

backToSales will loop to verify it reaches the sales screen. openSales uses am start, so it never triggers stray swipes. It also returns early if already on the sales screen. The second test's top card, 글1, is reachable by walking up from the bottom.

Eight walk passes are sufficient for the three items. The third test correctly skips an item missing from the list. The price-only order test processes both items on one screen without restarting, since the screen stays the same after the back action. The dead-tap case is still being considered.

priceOne returns skip when the menu fails to open, which removes the item from pending and breaks the loop cleanly. The reserved test skips without tapping or calling backToSales, so the loop exits immediately once the pending set empties.

scrollToEdge uses dumpXml on page zero rather than settledXml. backToSales invalidates the cache with an input keyevent, so stale dumps are avoided.

The early return for a known bottom edge must run before the swipe, not after. If the head card already matches the known title on page zero, the function returns immediately without an extra swipe. The implementation of scrollToEdge is now being drafted.

The drafted `scrollToEdge` returns immediately when the visible head card matches the known edge title after page zero. The first pass without a known edge performs three swipes and returns the bottom card.

The total swipe count is confirmed at nine, fitting within the twelve-swipe budget. The stuck threshold will remain unchanged. walkPass will return the settled bottom title so walkUp can pass it forward as the known edge for the next pass.

A successful bump moves the item to the top and changes the screen, so the pass should end and restart from the bottom. The existing walkUp already restarts the pass when progress is made and items remain, but it currently wastes swipes by walking all the way to the top first. The fix is to detect this screen change earlier and restart immediately.

The known-edge early return is mandatory. Without it, the pass would need thirteen swipes and exceed the budget. The early return also removes extra confirmation swipes after a mid-pass jump.

The home-screen detection logic is being refined. It will check for both "홈" and "나의 당근" text, and explicitly exclude screens like cooldown tips, bump sheets, and the sales menu to avoid false positives. This prevents stray swipes if the home check fails.

A `leftKarrot` helper is being added to detect when the app has left the Karrot package. It returns true for other apps like Kakao but false for the tip screen. This lets the walk recover by opening sales directly instead of pressing back.

The `backToSales` loop now retries up to four times. It checks for the sales screen, taps a discard button if present, opens sales directly when on home or another app, or presses back otherwise. If `openSales` fails to change the screen, the loop simply repeats.

The store test logic is being refined. Day-level matching will use a wider window. A five-day-old post should match, but a three-day-old one should not. When bumpAgoMinutes is zero, the code must use an exact timestamp instead of day rounding.

The `card.bumpAgoMinutes != null` check correctly handles a zero value, so the exact-timestamp path is taken instead of day rounding. A zero-day edge case is rare but acceptable.

The `nextBumpAt` observation heuristic is being validated against the passing tests. The first test passes because the 30-day cooldown estimate is later than the roughly 3-day prior estimate, so the later value wins. The second test is now being checked.

The second store test passes because the one-hour cooldown estimate is later than the roughly ninety-six-hour prior estimate, so the later value wins. The third test passes because the recomputed estimate matches the stored next value. ISO string equality is confirmed between the estimate function and the recordBump logic.

Only two store tests fail. The remaining issues are millisecond precision and timezone handling. Both Date.parse and toISOString preserve exact ISO strings, so strict equality comparisons work. The day-matching logic must handle the parser's conversion of days into minutes, while the test explicitly nulls minutes to test the day-level path.

The test card explicitly sets `bumpAgoMinutes` to null and `bumpAgoDays` to 5. This forces the day-level matching path. The real app would convert "5일 전" into minutes=7200, which would trigger the precise timestamp path and overwrite the stored bump time. The test avoids this by nulling the minutes field.

The store will treat a null `bumpAgoMinutes` paired with a set `bumpAgoDays` as day-level precision, matching the test exactly. Comments will be updated to reflect the new behavior. The `walkPass` function needs careful re-reading before editing, and the temporary `console.log` will be removed.

The reset check is sound. After a skip, backToSales returns to the list, so the after-key and before-key differ and the pass ends correctly. A "gone" state only occurs when the target card vanishes between the walk read and bumpOne read, which could indicate a window reset.

The walk flow is being validated against edge cases. A processed item that vanishes between the walk read and bumpOne read will not trigger a "gone" state because bumpOne finds the card on the same screen and proceeds to tap and back. If the first card on a screen is not pending but the second is, the second card is processed and the pass ends only if the screen resets. Reserved cards that are deleted without a back action leave the screen unchanged, so the loop continues for other cards and does not end the pass.

The action result handling structure is being drafted. The before-key is built from card titles. A "gone" result triggers a reread and breaks the loop. A "stop" result exits the pass and returns the bottom title. A "bump" result increments the tally.

The action result handling now counts priced-only bumps and skipped cards. After any action, the code re-reads the screen and compares the new card titles to the before-key. If the screen changed, the pass ends and restarts from the bottom. If the screen is unchanged, the loop continues.

walkPass will return the bottom card title as a string. Every return path must supply that title. The settledXml delay is acceptable because the codebase already uses it.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
The test file is short. The slowness comes from sleeps in the three fakeList tests and other delays.

The full suite may take 40–60 seconds. I will set a high timeout and implement the changes now. I am also verifying the known-edge early return logic against the failing tests. The "진전이 없으면" test correctly walks the entire list and stops. The order test scrolls to the static bottom edge, so the head stays unchanged and the stuck counter increments.

The order test logic is solid. I spotted a potential issue: returning immediately after a screen change might skip visible items if the list shifted slightly rather than jumping to the top.

The recovery logic is confirmed correct. Returning after a screen change is slower but acceptable. The first test's tapped order is verified. A guard will ensure backToSales fixes the screen after closing.

I realized that if the screen parse fails because we are on the home screen, the pass must end without swiping. I will make backToSales robust so it reliably returns to the sales list before the next pass begins. Otherwise scrollToEdge could swipe on the wrong screen and cause stray-swipe failures.

I will add an `ensureSales` helper to verify the sales list is active before any swipe. This prevents stray swipes if the screen detection is imperfect.

The `ensureSales` helper will wrap every swipe in `walkPass` and `scrollToEdge`. It opens the sales list if the screen is not active, which resets the fake list to top and prevents stray-swipe counts. The fake tracks swipes only when the mode is already "list".

The `ensureSales` guard must precede every swipe because the fake tracks stray swipes only when the mode is already "list". The `backToSales` fix is still required to prevent `leftApp` failures from pressing back while on the home screen. Both safeguards will be applied.

I will match the existing comment style in the source files. For the store test, I need to update `ingestedBumpedAt`, `ingestedNextBumpAt`, and their call site.

I will revert the temporary `console.log` I added to `swipeList`. I am checking whether `observedNext` could incorrectly preserve a stale `nextBumpAt` when `bumpedAt` is null. The `replaceFromPhone` logic deletes and reinserts records matched by title, so a prior listing with a null `bumpedAt` but a valid `nextBumpAt` from `recordCooldown` is kept if it is later. The seed estimate only sets `nextBumpAt` when both `bumpCount` and `bumpedAt` exist, so it cannot create a stale entry.

The `next_bump_at` logic is confirmed: it is null when `bumpedAt` is missing or `bumpCount` is absent. Shelf seeds have no bump count, so their next bump is null. When `replaceFromPhone` encounters a seeded listing with ago text, the prior next bump estimate is discarded and replaced by the new estimate. No existing tests depend on preserving later estimates across replacements.

I am now implementing the changes. I am refining the day-matching tolerance for `nextBumpAt`: if the absolute difference between the prior estimate and the day-rounded computed estimate is within 24 hours, the prior is kept. Otherwise it is discarded.

I chose the floor-based interpretation for `nextBumpAt`. A prior estimate is kept only if the listing age is within the same day as the day-rounded estimate. This treats "5일 전" as the event being 5 days old, not as being within 24 hours of exactly 5 days ago.

I will rewrite `walkPass` cleanly with `search_replace` and fix its return type and exit paths. I will also update the `walkUp` comment to describe the bottom-to-top scroll and the list returning to the top after a pull-up or window close.

The `walkUp` comment is being updated to describe the bottom-to-top scroll and the list returning to the top after a pull-up or window close. The pass limit of 8 is sufficient for the current test case, so it will not be changed.

The order test's price-only and bump items remain on the same screen after a back reset, so afterKey equals beforeKey and the pass continues. The dead-tap case deletes the pending item, re-reads the list, and breaks when pending is empty; the test expects no skipped count, so this behavior is correct. I am also checking the priceOne path when the menu fails to open.

The reserved path needs no changes. The known-bottom early return is confirmed: after a reset to the top, a single swipe reaches the bottom and returns immediately, satisfying the test comment without extra confirmation swipes.

The first pass cannot early-exit because no known bottom edge exists yet, so three swipes remain acceptable. I am now considering placing the `ensureSales` guard inside `swipeList` itself so it covers `scrollToEdge` as well, though `swipeList` currently lacks screen context.

I will place the `ensureSales` guard inside `swipeList` itself. It opens the sales list if the screen is inactive and aborts the swipe if the mode is still not list. This prevents stray swipes globally without extra calls. The extra screen dumps are acceptable.

The `ensureSales` guard is safe because `dumpXml` refreshes after a back keyevent, so the home screen is not cached. The `onSales` check correctly excludes the home and tip screens, so `openSales` will not fire during a stray swipe.

The home-screen recovery flow is verified. The first pass scrolls to the bottom, processes the top item, resets to home, and opens the sales list again. The second pass reaches the top and processes the remaining item. No stray swipes occur because every swipe stays on the list. The stuck-at-top guard is harmless since the titles change before the list reaches the top.

The store call site will pass `priorBumpedAt` and `priorBumpCount` to `ingestedNextBumpAt` alongside the new `bumpedAt` and `bumpCount`. The eight-pass limit is sufficient for the current test cases.

I am refining the `observedNext` logic. If `bumpCount` is zero or null, the function treats the existing `nextBumpAt` as an observed value rather than an estimate. This prevents invalid estimates when the bump count is missing or zero.

The `observedNext` logic is confirmed: an existing `nextBumpAt` is treated as an estimate only when `bumpedAt` exists, `count` is at least one, and the values match the formula. Otherwise it is treated as an observation.

A string mismatch from milliseconds is ruled out because `recordBump` stores the exact output of `estimateNextBumpAt`.

The test failure for count 3 is traced to the old estimate timestamp 1794394375000. The correct expected value is 2026-11-11T10:52:55.000Z.

The `backToSales` rewrite now checks for a "그만두기" discard button before pressing back. If the screen is the home screen, it opens the sales list instead of pressing back, preventing the app from exiting to the previous app.

The `needsSalesLink` helper is being defined to distinguish home and third-party screens from sales, cooldown, and edit forms. It returns true for home and non-owning app packages, and false for cooldown, bump sheet, and edit screens. The cooldown tip case is confirmed to press back rather than open sales.

The `walkPass` function is being rewritten to accept a `knownBottom` parameter. When the screen changes during a swipe, the function returns the last known bottom title so the next pass can resume from the correct edge. This prevents the pass from reading a new screen's last card as the bottom edge.

scrollToEdge returns the head card when it matches the known edge, and the walk loop will pass this known bottom into walkPass. The first page of a second pass is protected from an early return by the page > 0 check.

The walkUp loop now preserves the last known bottom title when walkPass returns an empty string. A trace confirms nine total swipes: one to reach the bottom, one to process 글9, one to return to the top, one to reach the bottom again, one to process 글5, one to return to the top, one to reach the bottom again, one to process 글4, and one final swipe to confirm the list is empty.

Cooldown skips correctly increment tally.skipped. The inner loop breaks after each handled item, preventing stale cards from being processed after a reset. The plan is complete and ready for implementation.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, relative to path, e.g. '*.ts', 'src/**/*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'. A pattern without '/' matches file names at any depth

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)
